Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: On MLS®: "Otter District" is one of eleven Langley sub-areas in the SnapStats data; "Langley" the board community combines the Township of Langley and the City of Langley, and this sub-area sits entirely on the Township side.

The Condos & Townhomes 0/0 combination is shared by three Langley sub-areas (Campbell Valley, County Line Glen Valley and Otter District), and Otter District and Campbell Valley are the two sub-areas with zero sales in both splits.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is none to concentrate. The board counted zero attached listings in the sub-area in September 2026. The structural reason, in one line: much of this district is Agricultural Land Reserve country, and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

Poppy Secondary, 23752 52 Ave, Langley. A school's presence nearby is not a catchment assignment. Poppy Secondary, no middle school shown) belongs to that address only and must not be extended to Otter District homes.

The ALR frame — the governing fact for much of this district: ALR land may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless it qualifies for an additional residence, and local governments may further regulate or restrict residences through zoning. The principal residence maximum is a total floor area of 500 m²; a secondary suite is permitted only when it is entirely contained within the principal residence (a separate or detached dwelling is not a secondary suite) and local bylaws permit it; and one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. ALR residences cannot be stratified. Parcel-level ALR status: confirmed on the ALC's ALR maps, not from the sub-area name.

Pad rent (the park): pad rent at Langley Grove Estates is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act: the rent increase limit for manufactured home site tenancies is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027.

(1) The card for the Langley Grove Estates unit at 52 24330 Fraser Highway carries a header price that conflicts with the different price stated at the end of its own listing text — the two prices in the same card do not match. (2) A 30 Avenue card advertises an open house for Sunday, October 25, 2026 — a date that had already passed by the November 1, 2026 reading while the card still showed Status: Active, so the open-house text is stale.
The guide places North Otter Elementary's catchment on both sides of Fraser Highway "on the SD35 map" and names Aldergrove Community Secondary as the secondary school. Poppy Secondary.

Col. William Otter; settler John William Best), the Otter Co-op history (Farmers' Institute formed 1922, store in 1946, became the Otter Co-op in 1979), Saint Alban's church moved in 1926, Otter Park's amenities and dawn-to-dusk hours, Fire Hall 7 – Otter at 3876 248 Street, the Bertrand Creek / Aldergrove aquifer notes, the Rural Plan (Bylaw No. 3250) Agro-Service Centre description, and the Highway 1 / 264 Street diverging-diamond rebuild with completion expected in 2027.

The park carries two civic addresses in the feeds. Langley Grove Estates appears at 3665 244 Street and at 24330 Fraser Highway in listing cards — the same park under both addresses, so a search run under only one address understates the park's shelf.
Two dwellings on a listing does not mean two legal dwellings. The approvals history is the diligence, not the listing text.

Tenure — fee-simple is the default: the district's acreages are freehold parcels under Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; zone assignment for a specific parcel comes from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource.
A park home on pad rent is not owned land, not fee-simple and not strata.

items.t: Otter District is a rural board sub-area on the south side of the Township of Langley — the Otter / Salmon River uplands country along 240 Street, 248 Street and 256 Street, south toward the US border side of the township. Salmon River, the neighbouring sub-area, lies directly to its north.

ALR housing frame: On ALR land the principal residence maximum is a total floor area of 500 m² (with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction); a secondary suite is permitted only when entirely contained within the principal residence; and one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. Parcel-level ALR status for any specific property: confirmed on the ALC's ALR maps, not from the sub-area name. Two first-page listings state ALR status in their own text — listing copy for those parcels only, not a district-wide designation. Manufactured homes on farm ground are dealt with only as ALC sources support (ALR Use Regulation / ALC policy routes).

The district's park looks like seniors product and is not: Langley Grove Estates has the clubhouse-and-amenities presentation buyers associate with 55+ parks, but its listings state no age restrictions — a buyer who assumes an age-restricted community from the presentation alone would be wrong. Otter District itself has zero known 55+ stock of any form.

A "coach house" here has a narrow legal meaning: Under Township Bylaw No. 2500, s.102, a coach house sits only within the second storey of a detached garage — a ground-floor detached suite on an Otter acreage is a different accessory unit with different rules, whatever a listing calls it.

faq.a: Within the ALC frame, one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on a property of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on a property over 40 ha, subject to Township bylaws; the principal residence itself is capped at 500 m², and a secondary suite must be entirely inside the principal residence (and within the Township's 120 m² suite cap).
faq.q: Can I build a second house on an Otter District acreage in the ALR?

faq.a: No. Township eligibility for 3–4 units under Bylaw 6020 requires Urban Containment Boundary location, municipal water and sewer, and a lot no larger than 4,050 m², and there is no 6-unit tier in the Township at all; a rural Otter lot that fails those tests falls to one unit plus a suite or accessory unit depending on zoning.
faq.q: Can I use the urban SSMUH numbers on an Otter acreage?

faq.a: No — it is a manufactured-home park at 3665 244 Street (also carded at 24330 Fraser Highway).
faq.q: Is Langley Grove Estates a condo complex?

faq.a: Within the ALC frame, one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on a property of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on a property over 40 ha, provided there is only one existing residence when construction begins and Township bylaws allow it; the principal residence itself is capped at 500 m², and a secondary suite must be entirely inside the principal residence.
faq.q: Can I build a second house on an Otter District acreage in the ALR?

faq.a: Not on ALR land within the ALC frame: ALR residences cannot be stratified — a strata plan deposit is a subdivision (SPA s. 239) and subdivision of agricultural land is prohibited unless the Commission permits it (ALCA s. 21(1); ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6).
faq.q: Can I strata-title the second home later?

faq.a: Almost never on this area: Township SSMUH eligibility requires Urban Containment Boundary location, municipal water and sewer, and a lot no larger than 4,050 m².
faq.q: Can I put 3–4 SSMUH units on an Otter acreage?

faq.a: Only through the Approving Officer under the Land Title Act, to the zone minimums (RU-2 and RU-3 need 8.0 ha for a new lot; RU-1 needs 1.7 ha) — and ALR land also needs Agricultural Land Commission approval to subdivide.
faq.q: Can I subdivide an Otter District acreage?

faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act.
faq.q: In Langley Grove Estates, do I own the land?

faq.a: No. Listings for the park state "no age restrictions" — it is an all-ages manufactured-home community at 24330 Fraser Hwy / 3665 244 St. The clubhouse, exercise centre and sauna/hot tub in its listing text do not make it a seniors park.
faq.q: Is Langley Grove Estates a 55+ park? It has a clubhouse.

faq.a: Within the ALC frame on ALR land: one additional detached residence without an ALC application at up to 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), provided Township bylaws allow it, and a suite only inside the principal residence (capped at 500 m²). Outside the ALR, Township SSMUH eligibility is narrow; most rural Otter lots fall to one unit plus a suite or accessory unit depending on zoning.
faq.q: Can I build a second home on an Otter acreage instead?

faq.a: The documented stock is freehold acreages and Langley Grove Estates park homes; a listing describing an acreage with two dwellings is an ALR second-dwelling item to diligence, not a duplex project.
faq.q: Is there a duplex development in Otter District I can buy into?

faq.a: And you would own the home as a chattel and rent the pad; you would not own land, and the mhpta — not the Strata Property Act — governs.
faq.q: Is Langley Grove Estates a 55+ park? Can I buy the land?

faq.a: No. Under Bylaw 2500 s.102 a coach house is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage — a fee-simple second unit, never strata.
